findings.title: [P1] Return `id`, not `userId`, to satisfy the declared `User` contract
findings.body: `loadUser` declares `Promise<User>` where `User = { id: string; name: string }` (`src/users.ts:7`), but the new return statement produces `{ userId: row.id, name: row.display_name }` (`src/users.ts:11`). The object literal omits the required `id` property and adds an undeclared `userId` property, so TypeScript rejects it (TS2741 missing property / TS2353 excess property), failing any type-checked build. Even in transpile-only setups, every successful lookup now resolves to an object without the declared `User.id`, silently breaking consumers that read `user.id`. This directly contradicts the PR's stated intent to preserve existing contracts. Either revert to `id: row.id` or, if the rename is truly intended, update the `User` type and all consumers in the same change (no in-repo callers currently exist, so the fix is confined to this line or the type declaration).
